text:
alex: opened a tiny docs PR to reconcile audit export examples and add a short migration checklist for Dedicated -> Private. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/3172
priya: nice. please clarify that "ingest TTL" is different from archival retention. customers kept asking which one controls query availability vs long-term evidence.
alex: added a short 'TTL vs archival' paragraph: ingest TTL = how long events are queryable in the live index; archival/export = separate JSONL evidence store. included example S3 export command.
jonah: legal called out the line 'we purge logs after 90 days' in the draft. can we rephrase to avoid implying unilateral data deletion without context? @legal-ops any suggested language?
legal-ops: prefer control-focused wording: "Logs are retained according to configured retention windows. Redwood supports export and archival workflows and can assist with legal holds or administrative retention requests." avoid absolute-sounding 'we purge' statements.
alex: updated the wording accordingly and left a concrete Console screenshot reference showing retention selection.
chris: automated link checks flagged a broken TS snippet link.
docs-bot: :warning: link-checker: 1 broken link: /sdk/examples/ts/audit-export.ts (404)
alex: that's a rename artifact on my local branch. replaced with an inline minimal TypeScript snippet and added a Python parity example:
```typescript
// minimal TS audit export (example)
import { AuditClient } from '@redwood/sdk'
const c = new AuditClient(process.env.REDWOOD_KEY)
await c.export({ scope: 'tenant:acme', since: '2025-01-01', destination: 's3://acme-audit-exports/' })
```
```python
# export audit events to S3 (example)
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
client.export(scope="tenant:acme", since="2025-01-01", destination="s3://acme-audit-exports/")
```
priya: can you also add a 4-step migration checklist for Dedicated -> Private? customers asked for simple steps: snapshot exports, confirm KMS keys, grant control-plane export perms, validate ingestion.
alex: added checklist bullets and a note that export artifacts are JSONL with a 'redwood_audit_version' field for tooling compatibility.
jonah: legal wants a short note that audit events containing tenant identifiers might require pseudonymization depending on customer policy.
legal-ops: confirm. suggested adding a hashing example and linking to the privacy playbook.
alex: added a tiny pseudonymization snippet (SHA256 tenant id) and a cross-link to /docs/privacy/pseudonymization. fixed the TS link and re-ran checks.
docs-bot: :white_check_mark: checks passed (link-check, lint, snippet smoke-run).
priya: nit: in the Python example change param name from 'dest_uri' to 'destination' to match SDK.
alex: updated. ready for reviews.
chris: lgtm from eng docs.
jonah: lgtm from security; I'll queue legal approval.
legal-ops: approved, please include the PR number in the compliance evidence bundle.
alex: merged. will add a brief release notes line for the next docs patch release. :tada:
